pattern.crimePattern: mother kills the tuk-tuk driver she believes killed her son in an unsolved hit-and-run, and bribes a witness
pattern.notes: Unsolved hit-and-runs are a real and painful pattern; no real case is depicted. Tone: Felister is a grieving mother, not a monster. Abdalla's guilt for the hit-and-run is stated as evidence, never as justification.

ob.text: A police patrol reports a tuk-tuk driver, Abdalla Swaleh (32), found slumped in his parked tuk-tuk on Mama Ngina Drive at 22:05. A tuk-tuk driver at the scene, Rajab Mwaringa, describes "a tall man in a cap" running away towards Likoni Road.

facts.text: Tuk-tuk driver Abdalla Swaleh was found slumped in his parked tuk-tuk on Mama Ngina Drive at 22:05.
At the scene, tuk-tuk driver Rajab Mwaringa told the patrol he saw "a tall man in a cap" run towards Likoni Road.
Abdalla was struck with his own tuk-tuk's tyre lever, kept under the seat.
His takings pouch is still on his belt, untouched.
Abdalla's phone: last payment at 21:28, KSh 200 from FELISTER MGHANGA, reference 'fare'. No calls after 21:20.
Mama Chiku: at about 21:30 a woman in a red kanga got into Abdalla's tuk-tuk "like a passenger". It drove a little way up and stopped. She never saw a tall man in a cap.
Mama Chiku: Rajab only arrived after the police, "about ten past ten".
Mama Chiku: last week Abdalla fought another driver, Omari Kai, over the Mama Ngina stage.
Mama Chiku was at her cart in full view of the drive from 18:00.
Records, Rajab's line: Bamburi mast until 22:02. Mama Ngina zone from 22:10.
Records, Rajab's line: an incoming call at 21:44 from FELISTER MGHANGA's number.
PesaPap, Rajab's line: 22:40, KSh 3,000 from FELISTER MGHANGA.
Garage receipt in the glovebox, 2 January: 'Front fork straightened, windscreen replaced — cash.'
Owner's sticker: the tuk-tuk belongs to S. O. Mbarak, daily hire.
Archive, OB 03/01/01: hit-and-run, Nyali Road, 23:50, New Year's night. Jeremy Mghanga, 19, died at the scene. "Three-wheeler, fled, no plate seen." Pending, no suspect.
Felister's red kanga was washed last night and is still damp this morning.
Felister's handbag: purse, ID, a photo of Jeremy. Nothing of Abdalla's.
Ali Bakari Mwamba: Said Omar Mbarak sat at the Makadara match committee from 19:00 to 22:30.
Omari Kai's own phone: a passenger paid him at 21:15 for a fare to Bamburi, and his phone stays on the Bamburi mast until 22:20.
Rajab: "At about 21:40 I saw a tall man in a cap hit him and run towards Likoni Road."
Rajab admits he saw nothing. Felister called him at 21:44, crying, and paid him KSh 3,000 to tell the police about a tall man in a cap. "She said he killed her boy."
Felister: she paid Abdalla a fare and rode along the drive at about half past nine.
Felister: "He was alive when I got out."
Felister, shown the old OB entry: "Eight months. Nobody came. Nobody looked. I looked."
Said: "I was at the football committee."
Said: Abdalla was two weeks behind on the daily rent for the tuk-tuk.
Said: in January Abdalla told him the damage came from "a pothole". "I believed him."
Kai: "I was on a fare to Bamburi."

interrogations.intro: Rajab stands by the patrol car, talking too fast. "Tall. A cap. He ran that way. I saw it all."
Felister opens her door before Amani knocks, a red kanga folded over her arm. "You came. Somebody finally came."

topics.reply: Eight months. Nobody came. Nobody looked. I looked.
She hands over the red kanga without being asked. "It's still wet. I washed it last night."
A mechanic told me in August. The second of January. A smashed front and a new windscreen, cash, no questions.

interrogations.intro: Said answers from the Makadara grounds, a whistle going behind him. "My tuk-tuk? What has he done to my tuk-tuk?"

topics.reply: Two weeks behind on the daily rent. Good driver, bad payer.
In January he told me he hit a pothole. I believed him. I fixed nothing. He paid himself.
Ask the committee secretary. I sat at that table all evening.

interrogations.intro: Omari Kai holds out his phone before he is asked. "Look. Bamburi. I was in Bamburi."

topics.reply: We fought over the stage. That's the stage. You don't kill a man for the stage.

interrogations.intro: Mama Chiku goes back to cutting coconuts so that her hands have something to do. "I saw what I saw. I didn't see a tall man."

topics.reply: Rajab? He came after the police. Ten past ten. Now he is telling the police a story.

contradictions.reaction: I didn't see anything. She called me crying. She gave me three thousand to say it. She said he killed her boy. I have a boy too.

words.text: she believed his tuk-tuk had killed her son
a road-rage fight with a stranger

prosecutor.pass: Two files, then. His and her son's. Get me the garage.
fail: Doesn't hold up. There is no tall man in a cap. Who paid the witness?
No. A rival in Bamburi and an owner at a committee table. Who got into that tuk-tuk at half past nine?

prosecutor.pass: The second of January. A smashed fork and a new windscreen. She wasn't wrong about that.
fail: She did it. But the fare was paid in advance. Look further back. Much further back.
That reason belongs to someone else, or to a man who doesn't exist.

proof.concludes: At 21:28 Felister paid Abdalla a fare. At 21:30 a woman in a red kanga got into his tuk-tuk, and it stopped up the drive. Felister says she rode with him.
The tall man in a cap was invented. Rajab was in Bamburi until 22:02; Felister called him at 21:44 and paid him KSh 3,000 at 22:40.

Abdalla's tuk-tuk was repaired, for cash, the day after Jeremy Mghanga was killed by a three-wheeler that fled. Felister is Jeremy's mother. Her red kanga was washed that night. Felister Mghanga killed him.

eliminations.why: Said sat at the Makadara committee from 19:00 to 22:30.
Kai was on a fare to Bamburi from 21:15 and stayed on the Bamburi mast until 22:20.
Mama Chiku was at her cart in full view of the drive.
The fare was paid in advance by phone.
His takings are untouched, and nothing of his is in her bag.
The unpaid rent is Said's grievance, and Said was at the committee table.
The stranger was invented by a bribed witness.

reconstruction.text: New Year's night, 23:50. A three-wheeler hits Jeremy Mghanga on Nyali Road and drives off. The file stays open, and empty.
2 January. Abdalla's tuk-tuk comes into a garage with a bent front fork and a smashed windscreen. Cash. No questions.
August. A mechanic tells Felister. For weeks she watches Abdalla's stage.
21:28. She pays him two hundred shillings for a ride along the drive. When he stops, she asks if he remembers New Year's night. He laughs.
21:44. She calls a driver she knows and pays him three thousand to describe a man who was never there.

afterVerdict.beat: OB 03/01/01 is reopened. The garage receipt closes it: Abdalla Swaleh's tuk-tuk killed Jeremy Mghanga. Halima files both.

tier1.line: Ask the coconut seller what she saw, and when the witness arrived.

tier2.line: A fare paid at 21:28, and a woman in red climbing in at 21:30.

tier1.line: What did the tuk-tuk need fixing in January? Then search the archive for her name.

tier2.line: A smashed front on 2 January. A hit-and-run on New Year's night. Her son.
